items.type: {P : Type u_1} → [inst : Preorder P] → P → {ι : Type u_2} → [Encodable ι] → (ι → Order.Cofinal P) → ℕ → P
items.informal_description: A sequence in a preordered set $ P $ defined recursively: starting with an initial element $ p $, each subsequent term is either the previous term or an element from a cofinal subset $ \mathcal{D}(i) $ that is greater than or equal to the previous term. Specifically, for $ n+1 $, if the decoding of $ n $ yields an index $ i $, the next term is chosen as an element above the current term in the cofinal subset $ \mathcal{D}(i) $; otherwise, it repeats the previous term.

items.informal_name: Membership of Encoded Index in Cofinal Subset for Sequence Construction
items.type:
∀ {P : Type u_1} [inst : Preorder P] (p : P) {ι : Type u_2} [inst_1 : Encodable ι] (𝒟 : ι → Order.Cofinal P) (i : ι),
  Order.sequenceOfCofinals p 𝒟 (Encodable.encode i + 1) ∈ 𝒟 i
items.informal_description: For any index $i$, the $(\text{encode}(i) + 1)$-th term of the sequence constructed from $p$ and $\mathcal{D}$ is an element of the cofinal subset $\mathcal{D}(i)$.

items.informal_name: Element above a given element in a cofinal subset
items.type: {P : Type u_1} → [inst : Preorder P] → Order.Cofinal P → P → P
items.informal_description: Given a cofinal subset $ S $ of a preordered set $ P $ and an element $ x \in P $, this function returns an element $ s \in S $ such that $ x \le s $, using the axiom of choice to select such an $ s $.

items.informal_name: Existence of Strict Order Series Bounded by Coheight
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Preorder α] (a : α) {n : ℕ}, ↑n ≤ Order.coheight a → ∃ p, RelSeries.head p = a ∧ p.length = n
items.informal_description: For any element $a$ in a preorder $\alpha$ and any natural number $n$ satisfying $n \le \text{coheight}(a)$, there exists a strict order relation series $p$ of length $n$ with $p.head = a$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Strict Order Chains of Bounded Length in Preorders
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Preorder α] (a : α) {n : ℕ}, ↑n ≤ Order.height a → ∃ p, RelSeries.last p = a ∧ p.length = n
items.informal_description: For any element $ a $ in a preorder $ \alpha $ and natural number $ n $ satisfying $ n \leq \text{height}(a) $, there exists a finite chain of strict order relations $ <$ of length $ n $ whose last element is $ a $. The height of $ a $ is defined as the supremum of lengths of all such chains ending at elements $ \leq a $.

items.informal_name: König's Lemma for Partial Orders: Infinite Chains from Finitely Many Successors
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : PartialOrder α] [IsStronglyAtomic α] {b : α},
  (∀ (a : α), {x | a ⋖ x}.Finite) → (Set.Ici b).Infinite → ∃ f, f 0 = b ∧ ∀ (i : ℕ), f i ⋖ f (i + 1)
items.informal_description: Let $ (\alpha, \leq) $ be a partially ordered set. Suppose that for every element $ a \in \alpha $, the set of immediate successors $ \{x \in \alpha \mid a \lessdot x\} $ is finite, and that the upward-closed interval $ [b, \infty) = \{x \in \alpha \mid b \leq x\} $ is infinite. Then there exists an infinite sequence $ (f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}} $ in $ \alpha $ such that $ f_0 = b $ and $ f_n \lessdot f_{n+1} $ for all $ n \in \mathbb{N} $.
